title: Vikas Khanna's Unstoppable Year: From TIME 100 to Harvard's Stage to a Chai Empire
excerpt: The Amritsar-born chef's 2026 has been a masterclass in turning cultural pride into global influence — and he is just getting started.
body:
In the small constellation of Indian chefs who have made the West sit up and pay attention, Vikas Khanna has always been an outlier — a Michelin-starred restaurateur who also directs films, a humanitarian who organized 30 million meals during COVID-19, and a judge on *Celebrity MasterChef India* who speaks as comfortably to home cooks in Amritsar as to fine-dining critics in Manhattan. But even by his standards, 2026 has been extraordinary.

In April, TIME magazine named Khanna to its prestigious TIME100 list of the world's 100 most influential people. The tribute, written by James Beard Award-winning chef Eric Ripert of Le Bernardin fame, called Khanna one of the most "powerful cultural voices" of his generation — a man whose influence "extends deeper than fine dining." It was the first time an Indian chef had appeared on the list in years, and it set the tone for a season of recognition that has yet to slow down.

## From Amritsar's Bylanes to Harvard's Stage

Last week, the South Asian Association at Harvard University honored Khanna as its Person of the Year. Standing on a stage in Boston, the chef who once labored in tiny kitchens in India before earning a Michelin star in New York was visibly moved. "What a milestone for Indian cuisine," he said. "To be named Person of the Year by Harvard University's SAA is beyond words. This recognition is not just an award — it's a promise."

The honor is not merely ceremonial. Khanna's restaurant Bungalow, which opened in New York's East Village in March 2024 as a tribute to his late sister Radhika, has become one of the city's hardest reservations to get. *The New York Times* awarded it three stars. The Michelin Guide gave it a Bib Gourmand in its first year. Bloomberg called it the "most exciting" new Indian restaurant in the city. At Bungalow, guests are greeted with a Gangajal ritual — holy water — and a menu that treats Indian cuisine not as an ethnic curiosity but as high art.

## Building an Empire, One Cup at a Time

Khanna is also thinking beyond his own kitchen. This weekend, Bungalow Hospitality Investments — a new investment platform Khanna co-founded with restaurateur Jimmy Rizvi — announced a strategic investment in Kolkata Chai Co., the New York-born chai brand founded in 2019 by first-generation Bengali-American siblings Ani and Ayan Sanyal.

The deal goes beyond money. Kolkata Chai's signature masala chai will now be served across Bungalow Hospitality Management's growing New York portfolio, including GupShup and the soon-to-open Punjab Meet House. Limited-edition collaborative menus are planned for the fall.

Kolkata Chai has already attracted notable backers — comedian and actor Hasan Minhaj joined as an investor and business partner in 2024, calling it an opportunity to give chai its "matcha moment." With Khanna now on board, the brand sits at the intersection of culinary credibility and cultural storytelling, exactly where South Asian food needs its champions.

## What It Means for the Diaspora

For NRIs who grew up watching Khanna on *MasterChef India* or reading his 41 cookbooks, these milestones carry a personal weight. Khanna has never shied away from his roots — his restaurant is named after the bungalow houses of Indian country clubs, his films center on Indian women's stories, and his Feed India initiative reached 135 cities during the pandemic.

The RPH College of Hospitality Management in Mumbai has launched a scholarship in his name, open from the 2026-27 academic year. The message to the next generation of Indian chefs is clear: the world is ready for you.

"Being on the TIME100 list is a matter of immense pride for me," Khanna said in April. "This achievement is a victory for India and our culinary legacy." Half a year later, the victory keeps compounding.
